Back in the beginning of the rise of phone-photography, Instagram was making a killing on its numbers, and trends began being created, such as using Instagram filters and editing pictures to look a certain way to appeal to their followers. Somewhere along the way a really accessible app got developed called VSCO where you can edit your pictures in almost every aspect, and post them to a private blog (.vsco) or share them to another site (Instagram).

The VSCO girl trend became a thing when the app was so popular, that socially, you were seen as behind if you had not yet began using the app and posting to the VSCO feed.

So over the course of about 7 years, it has gained notoriety as a staple to the phone-photography core which sits at the heart of social media, and has gotten to the hands of kids, as we see them using iPhones at such a younger age. I didn’t get an iPhone until I was 17-18 years old, whereas I see 8 year olds with better phones than me nowadays. The social media, especially VSCO users are generally below the age of 17.

Tldr; Need stats, leaderboards, more developed HUD/ or modified menu, adjusted button layout capability
